Restricting to pairs whose images stay in their fibers and translating gives submarginals dominated by the original marginals. The common residual mass e is completed by the product divided by e, with the zero case handled separately.

The interpolation weights have base barycenter z₀, so the base-linear part of the shear cancels and the midpoint shift is exactly h. For the central pair both shifts already equal h. Retained atoms remain exact. The two remaining positive measures have the same mass e, giving the specified total variation bound.

Failure of either endpoint to remain in its fiber is bounded by the sum of the two marginal losses. Their sum uses α+β=2μ and yields the exact overlap bound with factor 2/M. Reversal preserves each overlap volume.

The pair strata are finitely many clopen base pairs and the midpoint formula is continuous on them. Thus closed-cap maxima exist on the coupling space, and the finite dual identifies V with the infimum of capacities on the median fiber. Off the fiber a separating cap gives zero for both. Aligning each through-center cap by translation bounds each finite mixture and the infimum of individual caps in both directions.

On each line parallel to the translation, interval overlap loses min(displacement length, slice length). Integrating and substituting tb for the shear gives the directional bound before infimizing over b, with counting measure in d=1.
